title: How McRae became "Mr. Bear" and made "Walking the Blues"
summary: At Glover's urging McRae worked with Jack Dupree, devising a record where he walked on a board while Dupree played blues.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: When you recorded as Mr. Bear, one thing, where did that name come from?

When I was writing for King -- This is when I was telling about the years (inaudible) -- after we did -- before Bob Rolontz -- Glover had -- I had did the things for Wynonie Harris. And when Glover got over there he say, "Well" --

You know, I was writing -- doing some rock and roll. You see, I did a lot of things with Glover on different artists that he had over there.
He told me one day -- he says, "Why don't you do something with Jack Dupree?" So I didn't know what --
I says, "Okay, I'll do something."
Because with me I was just a -- if you ask me to do something, then I'll just go out and try to pick up some work -- what can I do with this artist.
And I -- be flexible. You know, you had to be flexible because the changes -- big bands was going out, little bands were coming in, and Ala Freed was in town.
He was coming in with all this rock and roll -- rhythm and blues stuff was coming in.
So he says why don't you do something with Jack Dupree. (Inaudible). So he introduced me to Jack Dupree.
And I had checked on Jack and found out some of the things he had did. I say, "Okay."
But knowing Jack couldn't read or write

too good, so I say, "I'll tell you what I'm gonna do. I'll come up to your house, we'll sit down and we'll talk."
And we got the idea of this Walking The Blues thing. I say, "We'll do a record call "Walking The Blues".

I was telling him -- I say, "Do you know -- you ever been south, you know, late in the summer and these guys walking down the road trying to get home? The sun go down and the guy got a guitar around his back, another guy got a jug (inaudible)." a little crazy thing "Yeah," just talking (inaudible), you know. He says, "Yeah."
I say, "Okay." we gonna (Inaudible) call this thing "Walking The Blues". So he says, "What we gonna do?"
So I told him, I say, "When we get to the studio, I got an idea. I'm gonna get some -- a floor, like a hardwood floor guys dance on."
The guy say, "Yeah, we got one (inaudible)."
So I say, "Now what you do -- I'm gonna start walking on this board. You start playing some

blues -- I'm gonna be talking to you and when I throw you a line, you answer me back but keep the blues going -- you be walking just like you walking down the road."
All right, Jack gets to the studio -- him and his wife had a little argument about something. About a dress or something.
So he gets in the studio and started playing the blues and I started walking. He say, "Yeah."
I says, "I'm Mr. Bear." Jack Dupree and Mr. Bear. I don't know where I got that name, because I was called (inaudible) Mr. Bear.

Jack (inaudible) say, "Okay." Jack started talking -- when he started talking about some blues -- about Walking The Blues or something, and everything he's telling me don't rhyme what we had walked out -- worked out, you know.
We had worked out something -- what I'm gonna throw to him and he's gonna throw to me (inaudible).
But he started talking about something else. And I'm walking and the engineer is getting the
sound of me walking together and him playing the piano and talking.
So he say, "Don't say nothing, let him keep on," you know. So he walked -- he talked all the way through the record. I didn't get a word in.
